title: Attention page lifecycle and decode QoS controller
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Background: As more tenants run long-context workloads on the hosted runtime, we see recurring p99 decode spikes caused by churn and suboptimal page residency decisions in the paged attention layer. Current eviction heuristics are reactive and treat all pages uniformly; this leads to kernel mis-matches at decode time, frequent synchronous prefill from cold storage, and transient GPU stalls.

Objective: Implement a Page Lifecycle Manager and a Decode QoS Controller that together: 1) track page cohorts by access pattern and kernel compatibility; 2) make pro-active residency and compaction decisions; and 3) steer decode waves with QoS signals so we can trade a small increase in median latency for significant reductions in p99 and reduced synchronous prefill events.

Scope: Runtime changes in the paged-attention allocator, a lightweight in-memory cohort classifier, decode scheduler hooks to honor QoS priorities, telemetry, and an end-to-end benchmark harness. No API changes. Backend-safe rollout (flagged).
acceptance_criteria: p99 decode latency reduced by >= 35% on the long-context baseline (100k synthetic traces)
Synchronous prefill events per hour reduced by >= 60% on heavy churn workloads
No increase in median token latency > 10% across sampled production routes
Feature gated and can be toggled per-tenant via runtime config
Automated bench that reproduces prior p99 spikes and demonstrates improvement included in repo

decisions: Classifier design: use a sliding-window recent-access histogram (128-sample) instead of full LRU timestamps to keep memory and compute bounded
Cohorts: three-state lifecycle chosen to limit state explosion and simplify migration (hot -> warm -> transient)
Eviction: prefer compaction + coalescing of warm pages over immediate eviction when high decode pressure is observed
Prefill policy: prefetch warm pages opportunistically during GPU idle windows; fetch transient pages only on demand
QoS signals: routes expose a priority integer and recent token SLA; scheduler will lower admission for low-priority traffic under memory pressure
performance_goals: Reduce synchronous stall time attributable to cold-page prefill from median 12ms to <4ms
Cut p99 token decode latency on churny workloads by >= 35%
Decrease GPU memory thrash rate (evictions/sec) by >= 40% under mixed-tenancy tests
test_plan: Unit tests for lifecycle state transitions and eviction timers
Microbench: synthetic client that generates churn patterns (short bursts of long contexts) - run on perf lab hardware matching production GPU types
Integration: end-to-end runtime bench that measures token latency and prefill counts across 100k traces
Canary: 5% traffic for 48h with telemetry comparing p50/p95/p99 and prefill/error rates
Failure tests: force PLM to misclassify and ensure decode QoS degrades gracefully (no crashes, bounded latency regression)
rollout_plan: Feature flagged behind runtime 'plm_decode_qos' per-tenant toggle
Start in perf lab; run A/B for 72h
Canary: enable for internal beta tenants (non-customer) for 24h
Expand to 5% production routes and monitor SLOs for 48h
If green, 25% for 24h, then 100% over a week
If regressions observed, auto-rollback and capture traces for investigation

Alert: decode-p99 increased > 20% from baseline for 10m
